text:
ana: FYI brought up Gemma-lite -> Llama-sim export + nf4 quant. short prompts look identical, but long-context (>1500 tokens) produces a collapsed repetition: "and then and then and then" loop.
sam: yikes. any conversion flags or tokenizer mapping used?
ana: pipeline was: gemma ckpt -> hf format -> llama-adapter. used rotary adapter with per-head scaling and our quantize_nf4 script. commands pasted: 
```
python export_hf.py --in ckpts/gemma --out /tmp/gemma_hf --tokenizer gemma-toki.json
python adapt_llama.py --hf /tmp/gemma_hf --out /tmp/llama_sim --rotary per_head_scale --vmap mappings/vocab_shift_v5.json
python quantize_nf4.py --model /tmp/llama_sim --calib datasets/longcal
```
ops-bot: deploy:quantize-nf4 job started id=job-7642

sam: can you grab a small logits trace and the token ids around the first repeat?
ana: sure, here's an excerpt: 
```
# tokens around loop
[102, 589, 44, 102, 589, 44, 102, 589]
# token strings
["and", "then", ",", "and", "then", ","]
# prob snapshot pre-loop -> loop
pre_loop_top1: 0.09 -> loop_top1: 0.81
pre_loop_entropy: 3.5 -> loop_entropy: 0.8
```
jin: that jump looks like identity-lock. my top two suspects: (A) vocab mapping created aliasing where punctuation tokens get mapped to text tokens (b/c shift) so self-attention keeps retrieving the same kv entries; (B) rotary index/permutation mismatch when converting head ordering (we sometimes swap head groups between Gemma and llama-sim).
sam: have you tried re-exporting with a vmap that has tokens_shift=0? also try toggling ROT_PHASE sign or using headwise vs per-head. small flip often breaks the loop.
ana: I re-ran with mappings/vocab_shift_v0.json (no shift) and the loop frequency dropped but didn't disappear. still worse than hosted Gemma. attached eval-bot output.
eval-bot: run_id=ev-176220-12
```
benchmark: longctx-stability
model: gemma->llama_sim-nf4
metrics:
  ppl_1k: "11.8"
  ppl_2k: "15.4"
  ppl_3k: "42.1"
  repeat_rate_1.5k+: "0.36"
  delta_vs-hosted: "-0.18"
```
jin: PPL at 3k still high. can you try a quick runtime shim: when reading kv entries, right-shift the kv index by the tokens_shift value (configurable env e.g. KV_INDEX_SHIFT). if that reduces repeat_rate it's definitely kv-key aliasing.
sam: I'll code a tiny patch for the runtime to support KV_INDEX_SHIFT and a debug flag to log kv key->token mapping when a repeat is detected.
nana: will run that now with KV_INDEX_SHIFT=5 (matches v5 mapping) and deterministic seeds.
nana: quick update after 30m run: with KV_INDEX_SHIFT=5 repeat_rate dropped to 0.05 and ppl_3k improved to 18.2. looks promising. posting the logs to the triage board.
sam: nice. sounds like converter should normalize token ids (strip the shift) during export so runtime doesn't need hacks. but runtime flag is a useful stop-gap. jin: can you add a unit test that encodes an alternating token probe and asserts no collapse for first 3k tokens?
jin: yes, adding test and an export sanity check for vocab_map.tokens_shift==0. also will run the same export->qwen-sim path to see if Qwen's tokenizer masked it.
nana: thanks all. follow-ups: 1) PR to converter to apply inverse mapping during export 2) runtime KV_INDEX_SHIFT flag as temporary 3) unit test in export pipeline 4) run full suite against hosted Gemma to measure delta. pinging #eng-ml-rooms for a short sync in 15m. :rocket:
